cells.tense: The fire is being tended well, and an ending here is being carried instead of feared.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Wonder what comes after this ending, then make a first move toward it — the kind of move you'd make if you already knew it was time.
cells.core:
You tend things well. What's ending here isn't being fought or hurried — you're holding it through its last stretch and the ones near you can feel how steady that is. The staying is doing its work: you keep something in its final season without letting that season become the whole story.

When you can feel what's finished and stay curious about what's next, it's because the experience has been digested rather than filed. You're free to try something you can't fully picture yet. The point isn't to decide the next chapter. It's to reach toward it and shift an inch. That's what keeps tending from becoming waiting.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry this ending and still lean toward what's next.
cells.place: where what is finished is cleared away

cells.tense: Something is going to be pushed through before it has finished ending.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Before pushing anything forward, tell whoever needs to hear it the one true hard thing about where this stands — gently, once, then no more.
cells.core:
You can feel the ending coming and your instinct is to get ahead of it — to start building the next thing while this one is still up, to force the clearing before it's finished clearing. From the outside that reads as hurry, and the people still inside the ending feel shoved.

What's needed here is the opposite of speed. Timing. Say the true hard thing about where this stands — not to force a decision, just to say it — gently, once. Then stop talking. Don't repeat it, don't explain it twice. Whatever can be heard gets heard the first time. Saying it plainly lets an ending happen at its own pace instead of yours.
cells.sheetLine: The push forward is a way of not letting it end.
cells.place: where what is finished is cleared away

lint.detail: the ask carries no word of the place — the same ask would serve any seat

cells.tense: A door has already closed and the person is still standing at it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Sort through what you're still tending and let a finished piece go — a habit, a role, a yes you keep giving out of habit. Keep what still feeds you.
cells.core:
Something already ended, and part of you is still at the doorway — tending a fire that's gone out, saying yes to something you've stopped feeling. The drive hasn't disappeared. It's just pointed at what's over, and it's running on nothing there.

There's nothing to charge up in that spot. What gets you moving is the clearing itself: knowing what to let go of, and doing it without ceremony. Let a finished piece go. Not because you finally feel like it — because it's over, and releasing it makes room. What still serves, you keep. That's not the loss of your drive. That's where it starts moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You're still tending a fire that already went out.
cells.place: where what is finished is cleared away

cells.tense: The ending is already happening and the person is telling it as something that happens to them.
cells.act: force the change into reality by steady effort
cells.ask: Look at what's already over and call it something you finished, not something done to you. Then push the next real inch through — an email, a cleared box, a call.
cells.core:
You're already the one ending this. The clearing is underway — things have fallen, structures have shifted — and the account you give is that it happened around you. It didn't. You've been moving it an inch at a time, steadily, the way anything actually gets rebuilt. That steadiness is the same drive you'd name if someone asked you what you're good at.

The work is seeing it. What's already over is something you finished, not something done to you. Then push the next real inch through — an email sent, a box cleared, a call made. Nothing ceremonial. The step doesn't need to be big. It needs to be yours, which it already is.
cells.sheetLine: You ended it, steadily, and you haven't said so.
cells.place: where what is finished is cleared away
